newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Heavy rains in S.Africa force evacuations.
newsitem.headline: Heavy rains in S.Africa force evacuations.

text.p: Heavy rains across South Africa have caused flooding in some towns, forcing families to evacuate their homes, rescue officials said on Friday.

In KwaZulu-Natal province 50 people were evacuated from their homes and businesses in Ladysmith after 120 mm (4.7 inches) of rain fell over 24 hours causing the Klip River flowing through the centre of the town to burst its banks.

"The river is currently at 8.3 metres (27 feet) and if we have more heavy rains without the river subsiding we could have one of the worst floods ever," Ladysmith protection services spokesman Koos Breedt told Reuters.
A local infantry battalion has been called in to help with the evacuations and to prevent looting of abandoned shops, he said.

In the industrial province of Gauteng a number of shacks were evacuated in Alexandra when the Jukskei River rose above two metres (6.5 feet) and burst its banks after heavy downpours across Johannesburg, emergency services spokesmen said.
Rainfalls of over 100 mm (four inches) caused a number of rivers in the eastern parts of Free State province to burst their banks but no incidents were reported, police said.
The Durban weather bureau has predicted rainy conditions will continue across the eastern parts of the country through the weekend before beginning to clear early next week.
